headline: Kothari Petrochemicals receives NSE no-objection to amalgamation of Kothari Sugars and Chemicals
sum: Kothari Petrochemicals Limited has received NSE Observation Letter conveying no objection to the proposed Scheme of Amalgamation of Kothari Sugars and Chemicals Limited into itself. The merger marks a regulatory milestone in the scheme approval pathway, with stock exchange clearance now secured.
implication: Stock exchange observation letter (non-objection) is a gatekeeping approval for listed-company schemes of amalgamation under NCLT jurisdiction; NSE clearance signals completion of the pre-NCLT regulatory phase, though final court sanction and RoC filing remain pending.
detail: Kothari Petrochemicals Limited, listed on NSE, has notified the exchange of receipt of an Observation Letter from NSE confirming no objection to the proposed amalgamation scheme. Under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, listed companies must disclose material events to the exchange; NSE's no-objection letter is a prerequisite before the scheme can proceed to the NCLT for sanction. The merger contemplates the absorption of Kothari Sugars and Chemicals Limited into Kothari Petrochemicals. No consideration amount, share exchange ratio, or expected completion date is disclosed in the NSE announcement.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015, Regulation 30
framework.note: Mandates disclosure of material events (including receipt of regulatory no-objection for schemes) to stock exchange; NSE observation letter triggers this disclosure obligation.

framework.ref: Companies Act 2013, Section 391–394 (Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation)
framework.note: Statutory framework for amalgamation of companies; requires NCLT sanction and creditor/shareholder meetings; NSE no-objection does not obviate NCLT jurisdiction.
Procedural rules governing NCLT applications for scheme sanction; NSE clearance is a precondition but not a substitute for NCLT approval.
Prescribes form and procedure for filing schemes with Registrar of Companies; applicable post-NCLT sanction.
Provides tax neutrality for amalgamations meeting specified conditions; transferee may carry forward losses of transferor if conditions met.

framework.ref: Reserve Bank of India (Foreign Exchange Management) Regulations 2015 (if cross-border element)
framework.note: If either party has foreign shareholding or NRI stake, additional RBI/FEMA compliance may apply.

framework.ref: Competition Act 2002, Section 5 (CCI Approval – if applicable)
framework.note: CCI review required if combined entity's asset/turnover thresholds trigger merger jurisdiction; no mention in NSE disclosure suggests either party below threshold or joint filing already completed.
